Clara Reeve, The Old English Baron.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/clara-reeve/the-old-english-baron

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Clara Reeve, the author, died 1807.

First publication of the text used: 1778 (SE colophon: 'was published in 1778 by Clara Reeve'). Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Old_English_Baron) says the text first appeared anonymously in May 1777, and gives 1778 as the first publication under this title.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1777 or 1778, before 1923, so it is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (United Kingdom; Wikipedia infobox country: United Kingdom): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the last person named above. The last to die did so in 1807, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 1878.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
